text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for customer AcmeAnalytics — P1: Private VPC data-plane packet loss spike (control plane OK). Alert ID: PD-987654. link: https://pagerduty.internal/PD-987654

pagerduty: Trigger conditions: 10m sustained packet loss >6% from agent -> control-plane; autoscale attempts failing. Escalation policy: oncall -> netops -> eng.

sre-oncall-jamie: Acked. I'm on it — pulling control plane metrics now. Do we have evidence it's data-plane only? :thinking_face:

eng-oncall-sam: seeing normal control-plane API latency in metrics (0.12s), but dataplane retransmits up ~8% from Acme region-us-west-2. Agent heartbeats still present.

netops-arya: can you paste the agent -> controlplane path traceroutes? asking Acme if anything changed on their side (security groups, route tables). cc @cust-success-maria

cust-success-maria: pinged AcmeAnalytics. They say no config changes on their VPC. They're seeing failed requests from their app to our endpoint. Very noisy on their side.

sre-oncall-jamie: running quick traceroute from our egress proxies to Acme agent IPs, results show intermittent hops with 40-60% loss at a middle hop (maybe peer). Suspect transit provider or peering.

eng-oncall-sam: grabbing tcpdump from the onprem-agent host to confirm. running:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.22.33.44 and tcp -w /tmp/acme-pktloss.pcap
```

platform-k8s-lee: I can spin up a temporary egress via a different AZ/region for their traffic to test whether loss follows the path. Want me to route a percentage?

sre-oncall-jamie: Yes, please. Start with 10% of traffic to us-west-1 fallback pool and monitor. Add a header so we can filter logs: X-Inc-Experiment: vpc-failover-1.

netops-arya: Contacting upstream transit provider now (ticket opened). Sharing traceroute + loss samples. ETA ~15m.

eng-oncall-sam: pcap shows retransmits and DUP ACKs consistent with packet drops on the path, not application-level errors. confirms data-plane packet loss.

cust-success-maria: Acme asked for ETA and if we can failover. They approved a temporary regional failover.

sre-oncall-jamie: Implementing regional failover config: updating routing policy to split 10% -> us-west-1 fallback pool. Applying now. Watch logs for 502/timeout rate.

oncall-handoff-bot: automated note: route change runbook step invoked by jamie, runbook ref: https://runbook.internal/redwood/vpc-packetloss. Step ID: RB-142.

eng-oncall-sam: failover applied. initial check: error rate for Acme traffic dropped ~60% for the routed 10%. overall customer error rate down from 12% -> 4% (still elevated).

netops-arya: upstream replied: "investigating peering fabric, possible maintenance-induced flaps, will update." They've temporarily blackholed a suspicious neighbor; monitoring for collateral.

platform-k8s-lee: started a canary at 25% after seeing improvement. No crashes on our side.

sre-oncall-jamie: good. tagging this incident: customer-impact: partial (some requests degraded), mitigation: regional split + upstream ticket. open incident bridge?

cust-success-maria: Yes, open bridge and loop in Acme SRE. They want periodic updates every 10m.

sre-oncall-jamie: opening bridge now. Bridge link: https://meet.internal/incident/2004506789

pagerduty: PagerDuty note: incident acknowledged by sre-oncall-jamie. Next escalation window in 12m if PD-987654 not resolved.

netops-arya: provider reports a transient BGP flap causing ECMP imbalance; they believe mitigation (route dampening) is in progress. Monitor for 30m.

eng-oncall-sam: continuing pcap capture and will drop anonymized sample to the provider. Also enabling longer TCP timeouts for Acme route to reduce request-level failures.

sre-oncall-jamie: recording post-mortem tracking items: 1) improve detection for mid-path loss vs control-plane; 2) automate fallback split on spike detection; 3) document customer communication template.

oncall-handoff-bot: handoff note: night shift coverage scheduled. Current oncall (jamie) will hand off to sre-oncall-riley at 03:00Z. Riley, please review incident state and provider ticket PD-987654.

cust-success-maria: I'll update Acme with the bridge link and that we've applied partial mitigations. keeping them informed.

sre-oncall-jamie: summary update for bridge: impact reduced to partial; mitigation: regional failover traffic split (10% -> 25% canary) + upstream provider working on BGP dampening; next update in 10m.

netops-arya: provider update: "BGP dampening active; loss rates decreasing, monitoring. We'll confirm full restoration or route flaps suppressed in 20-30m."

eng-oncall-sam: finalized artifact: attached pcap and traceroute output to provider ticket. Also flagged to infra for possible permanent route preference change if recurrence.

sre-oncall-jamie: good work team. I'll keep incident open until provider confirms stable for 60m and Acme reports full recovery. tagging follow-ups in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:

oncall-handoff-bot: final system note: incident PD-987654 remains open. Next human handoff to sre-oncall-riley at 03:00Z.

cust-success-maria: confirmed Acme sees improved success rate; they'll stay on the bridge for the next hour. thanks everyone. :pray:
